purpose: Stress provider transitions, deferred state, reconciliation, durable lineage, replay and propagated error budgets without creating a production scheduler.

hypotheses.claim: Durable body and operation lineage can survive provider changes and regenerated backend topology without importing provider-private identity into programme authority.
hypotheses.falsified_if: A provider transition requires a backend topology identifier to preserve durable identity, changes a durable body without an explicit lineage event, or maps an ambiguous lineage silently.

hypotheses.claim: A bounded directional/manual-mill fallback can remain useful as accepted_pending state while being barred from STEP until an independently validated conventional B-rep is reconstructed.
hypotheses.falsified_if: The fallback must be treated as STEP-authoritative, its representation error is cancelled arithmetically during handoff, or reconciliation cannot preserve the durable body/operation context.

hypotheses.claim: Hard semantic/query boundaries alone permit pending-state growth proportional to boundary distance, while adding a finite pending-size threshold bounds that growth at measurable reconciliation cost.
hypotheses.falsified_if: A threshold does not bound the declared pending-state proxy, or the policy comparison does not account for its additional reconciliation work.

hypotheses.claim: Connectivity-dependent decisions can fail closed while material state is pending and resume after explicit reconciliation without silently discarding split/merge bodies.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Body selection/connectivity is allowed before pending material is reconciled, or a split/merge loses a durable body or lineage event.

hypotheses.claim: A mixed-provider revision chain can discard provider-private derived state and replay from durable programme authority to the same declared engineering invariant.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Replay requires provider-private state or the deterministic programme-level replay signature changes.

hypotheses.claim: RCS-023 conservative budgets can cross provider/reconciliation boundaries without reset, with breaches failing closed and positive material-removal intent remaining explicit under uncertainty.
hypotheses.falsified_if: A handoff resets accumulated error, widens the engineering requirement, converts an over-budget state to success, or classifies explicit positive removal as no change merely because uncertainty overlaps zero.

rules: reconcile at explicit semantic provider boundary
also reconcile when pending_state_units reaches 2 in the deterministic stress fixture
reconciliation_policies.note: The value 2 is a research-fixture threshold used to expose scaling behavior, not a frozen production tuning constant.

measurements: material volume/dimensions/surface-deviation invariant where inherited evidence exists
body count/connectivity and durable body IDs
semantic lineage events and explicit ambiguity
backend topology identifiers as diagnostics only
pending-state units and peak pending state
reconciliation count and deterministic work-unit cost
STEP eligibility/status with Layer-D qualification preserved

resource_measurement_scope.reason: RCS-025 isolates semantic/resource-policy behavior deterministically; RCS-026 owns Windows/Linux scale, soak and process resource qualification.
